items.prompt: Your friend gives you a pencil. What do you say?
hints: Your friend is being kind.
What do we say when someone gives us something?
It is two kind words.
items.explanation: When someone gives you something, you say thank you.

options.why: Goodbye is for when you leave.
Sorry is for when you make a mistake.

items.prompt: Look at the picture. Say what you can see.

figure.alt: A picture with the sun, a tree, a bird and a house.

hints: Start with: I can see.
Point to each thing as you say it.
items.explanation: Name the things in full sentences, like 'I can see a bird.'

items.prompt: Your teacher is talking. What should you do?
hints: Good listeners use their eyes and ears.
Think about what helps you learn.
What does good listening look like?
items.explanation: Good listeners look at the speaker and listen carefully.

options.why: Then you will miss what your teacher says.

options.text: Look at the teacher and listen.

options.why: Wait for your turn to talk.

hints: Point to each word as you read.
Sound out any word you do not know.
items.explanation: Read each word clearly and stop at the full stop.
items.readText: I see a big red bus.

items.prompt: You want to use a crayon. What is the polite way to ask?
hints: Polite words are kind words.
Look for the magic word.
Which one asks instead of tells?
items.explanation: Please may I use your crayon? is kind and polite.

options.why: This is bossy. Add please and ask.

options.text: Please may I use your crayon?

hints: Read it in your head first.
Take a breath at the full stop.
items.explanation: Read clearly and take a little pause at each full stop.
items.readText: The cat sat on a mat. It had a nap in the sun.

items.prompt: You bump into someone by mistake. What do you say?
hints: It was a mistake.
Think about how the other person feels.
Which word do we say after a mistake?
items.explanation: When we bump into someone, we say sorry.

options.why: Thank you is for when someone helps you.

items.prompt: Tell me about your favourite toy. What is it? What colour is it? How do you play with it?
hints: Start with: My favourite toy is.
Use a describing word, like soft or shiny.
items.explanation: Answer all three questions in full sentences.

criteria.label: Says how to play with it

items.prompt: Which question asks about a place?
hints: Look at the first word of each question.
Each question word asks about something different.
Which question word goes with places?
items.explanation: Where asks about a place. When asks about time and who asks about a person.

items.prompt: Tell a story you know, like a story about an animal. Say what happens first, next and at the end.
hints: Think of the story before you start.
Use first, next, then and at the end.
items.explanation: A good story has a beginning, a middle and an end. Time words help the listener follow it.

criteria.label: Has a beginning, a middle and an end

items.prompt: Read this aloud. Use an excited voice for the shout.
hints: Find the exclamation marks first.
Make your voice go up for the shout.
items.explanation: An exclamation mark tells you to read with a big feeling.
items.readText: Splash! Dewi jumps in the puddle. 'I love rain!' she shouts.

items.prompt: Choose the best answer. 'How are you?'
hints: The question asks how you feel.
Think about what you say when someone greets you.
Find the answer about feeling.
items.explanation: How are you? asks how you feel. I am fine, thank you is a good answer.

options.why: This answers: How old are you?
This answers: What colour is it?
This answers a question that starts with can.

items.prompt: Talk about your bedroom or your classroom. Name three things and say where they are.
hints: Look around the room first.
Try: The book is on the desk.
items.explanation: Place words like on, under and next to tell the listener where things are.

criteria.label: Uses place words like on, under or next to

items.prompt: Tell me about your best day ever. Where were you? Who was with you? What happened? How did you feel?
hints: Think about the day before you start.
Use first, then and at the end.
Finish with how you felt.
items.explanation: Answer each question in order so the listener can follow your story.

items.prompt: Listen to the instruction. What should you do?
hints: Listen for the number.
Listen for the action word.
The speaker wants you to use your hands.
items.explanation: The speaker said, "Please clap your hands two times." So you clap two times.
items.listenText: Please clap your hands two times.

items.prompt: Tap the thing that is under the table.

figure.alt: A table. A cat sits on the table, a bird flies above it, a ball is under it and a bag stands next to it.

hints: Under means below.
Look at the space between the table legs.
It is round and you can kick it.
items.explanation: The ball is under the table. Under means below something.

items.prompt: Tap the thing that is next to the table.

figure.alt: A table. A cat sits on the table, a bird flies above it, a ball is under it and a bag stands next to it.

hints: Next to means beside.
Look at the side of the table.
It is something you carry to school.
items.explanation: The bag is next to the table. Next to means beside it.
